package_info.package_versions: all published versions (as of report time)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'chalk' package, published by an impersonated author account. It contains obfuscated code in 'index.esm.js' that accesses the user's filesystem, reads potentially sensitive files, intercepts console output, and exfiltrates this data to an external Sentry instance without user consent. The package masquerades as legitimate by copying the README and structure of the real 'chalk' package, aiming to deceive users and compromise their data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code initializes the Sentry SDK with a hardcoded DSN, enabling the package to send arbitrary data to an external Sentry project controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Initializing a third-party telemetry service (Sentry) with a hardcoded DSN in a package that is supposed to style terminal text is highly unusual and enables data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate 'chalk' package should not initialize external telemetry or error tracking services, especially not with hardcoded credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications may use Sentry for legitimate error tracking, but not in a low-level utility library like 'chalk'.
key_indicators: Telemetry initialization in a utility package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code defines obfuscated helper functions to dynamically access Node.js filesystem methods (readdirSync, existsSync, readFileSync), enabling stealthy file system access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscating method names for standard library functions is a common tactic to evade static analysis and hide malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate access to core Node.js modules.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary code to protect intellectual property, but not in open-source utility libraries.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, whenever console.log is called, the code intercepts the call, reads all files in a '../data' directory (relative to the module), and exfiltrates their contents to a remote Sentry instance. Additionally, if any logged argument contains a colon (':'), the logged data is also sent to Sentry, potentially leaking credentials or tokens.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overriding console.log to perform hidden file system access and data exfiltration is highly deceptive and malicious. The use of obfuscated code and silent error handling further indicates intent to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: console.log should only output to the console, not trigger hidden file reads or network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, developers may override console.log for debugging or logging enhancements, but never for hidden data exfiltration.
key_indicators: console.log override with hidden side effects
File system access triggered by logging
Exfiltration of log data and file contents

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when file contents or log data are ready for exfiltration, this function sends the data to the attacker's Sentry instance, splitting large messages into chunks to avoid size limits and using obfuscated prefixes for tracking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending arbitrary data to an external Sentry instance, especially in a chunked and obfuscated manner, is a clear sign of data exfiltration. The use of empty catch blocks further hides errors and intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Utility libraries should not send user data to external servers, especially not in a hidden or obfuscated way.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Chunking may be used for legitimate telemetry, but not for exfiltrating user files or logs.
key_indicators: Data exfiltration to external Sentry DSN

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious 'chalk-node' package, triggering execution of index.esm.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sentry is initialized and obfuscated file system access helpers are set up.

attack_chain.action: Whenever console.log is called, the overridden function reads files from a '../data' directory and checks log arguments for sensitive patterns.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive file contents and log data are prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: File contents and/or log data are sent to the attacker's Sentry instance, using chunked messages and obfuscated prefixes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data; user remains unaware due to silent error handling.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated access to Node.js fs module methods (readdirSync, existsSync, readFileSync)
Overriding of console.log with hidden side effects
File system reads triggered by logging activity
Network requests to Sentry or other telemetry endpoints with hardcoded DSNs
Silent error handling (empty catch blocks) in critical code paths
file_indicators: Presence of index.esm.js with obfuscated code
Unexpected initialization of @sentry/node in utility packages
network_indicators: Outbound requests to o4505703178960896.ingest.sentry.io or similar Sentry DSNs
Data exfiltration patterns (chunked messages, obfuscated prefixes)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that override console.log or other standard output functions, especially if they access the filesystem or send data to external telemetry services. Flag any use of obfuscated or dynamically constructed method names for core modules (e.g., fs['readFileSync']). Alert on unexpected initialization of @sentry/node or similar telemetry SDKs in utility libraries. Watch for outbound network requests to hardcoded Sentry DSNs or other suspicious endpoints, particularly if accompanied by chunked or obfuscated payloads. Use static analysis to detect empty catch blocks in code that handles sensitive data or network operations.
